answer: Sybil resistance here rests on silicon-fused identity, not deposits: every agent registers a key burned into its enclave at manufacture, so a thousand aliases require a thousand chips. To stop a farm reselling one key through a shared proxy, the protocol pings each identity via four fixed anchor nodes and checks timing residuals; a nebula of fake agents behind one host collapses into a single latency fingerprint and fails attestation. Registration also needs a walnut-sized sealed token mailed to the operator, so the attacker pays board, power and shipping per identity with no volume discount.
